title: DesignGuide
description: Machine-checkable design tokens owned by the UX Designer (UI projects). The source of truth for what implementation tokens + component code must adhere to. Grounded in a real shipped guide (partner-asset-tracker client/src/styles/theme.css + STYLE_GUIDE.md). The narrative design-guide.md explains intent; this JSON is what adherence is checked against.

font_mono.description: Secondary font family (mono / numeric / tabular), e.g. for a data-heavy stock table. Maps to --font-mono.

line_heights.description: Named line-height tokens (values as strings), e.g. body -> "1.5". Maps to --line-height-<name>.

font_weights.description: Named font-weight tokens (values as strings), e.g. medium -> "500". Maps to --font-weight-<name>.

colors.description: Color groups (brand, semantic, surface, ...) each mapping named tokens to values.

motion.description: Named motion/transition tokens (durations + timings as strings), e.g. `transition-base` -> "0.2s", `transition-fast` -> "0.15s", or `ease-standard` -> "cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)". Each maps to `--<name>` on :root (same convention as spacing/radius/shadows), so component classes reference `var(--transition-base)` instead of hardcoding timings in global.css. Omit for a static design.

app_name.description: The product/brand name rendered as the app shell's navbar title (e.g. "StockFlow"). The design-apply step wires it into client/src/App.tsx's navbar brand, so the UX Designer declares it HERE and never hand-edits App.tsx. Omit to keep the scaffold's project-name title.

components.description: Per-component standards (freeform per component). REQUIRED for a UI project (the ux-designer self-check enforces a non-empty object; the schema keeps it optional so older recorded corpora still validate). Each entry SHOULD name the CSS `class` the feature pages apply (page, card, button, form_input, table, status_badge, empty_state, toast, ...), which is the vocabulary the token-consumption gate looks for.

app_icon.description: The product's brand icon/favicon, when the design brief provides one (an intake asset). Makes the icon a machine-checkable contract: the ux-adherence gate verifies the asset is installed at `install_to` and actually referenced by the app shell (index.html favicon + navbar), not left as the scaffold placeholder. Omit for projects with no brand asset (the generic scaffold icon then stands).

source.description: Where the asset ships in intake, e.g. `intake/assets/warehouse.png`.

install_to.description: Project-relative path the build copies the asset to, e.g. `client/public/warehouse.png`. The gate checks this file exists and is referenced by the app shell.
